title: German, Japanese and French Legation code telegrams at La Paz, copied by informers for the US Legation, which the FBI could not decipher
correspondents: German Legation La Paz ↔ Auswärtiges Amt Berlin (also German Embassy Buenos Aires → Berlin); Japanese Legation La Paz; French Legation La Paz; copies sent by US Minister Douglas Dawson to the State Department and passed to the FBI (Hoover)
shelfmark: NARA, RG 59, Central Decimal File 1940-44, 862.20224 ('German military activities in Bolivia', non-jacket case), sub-nos. c. 87-150; French Legation copies noted to 851.20224; known from the purport list, NARA naId 88161456 (frames 88162640-88162646)
folio_note: Purport list 862.20224 pp. 9-14: La Paz despatches #1194 (15 Oct 1941), #1201, #1231 (20 Oct), #1248 (23 Oct, 'Copies of Code telegrams to and from German Legation in La Paz'), #1249 (German Embassy Buenos Aires → Berlin), #1265 (twelve enclosures), #1304 (ten additional handwritten text copies), #1318 (eleven), #1325 (six), #1408 (11 Dec, German and Japanese Legations), #1512 (2 Jan 1942, twenty-two telegrams), #1537, #1541 (French Legation), #1620 (26 Jan 1942) and more; telegram #259 of 12 Dec 1941 ('German and Japanese coded messages sent to Department: valuable enough to warrant considerable risk assumed by informer'); Justice Dept (Hoover) 19 Dec 1941: 'Coded messages of the German Legation, La Paz, Bolivia: Returning copies of -, unable to decipher same'; War Department: 'very valuable'; Justice 7 Jan 1942: '79 German Code Messages: Transmits copy of message decoded' (one decoded).
status: Found in the slice L word-hit triage (agent_59.md) and confirmed from the purport list OCR (fetched 27 Oct 2026). Blocked on access: the 1940-44 decimal file 862.20224 is not digitised (only the purport lists are online). Dozens of telegrams were copied; the FBI returned the German Legation copies unread in Dec 1941, and only one of 79 later messages is noted as decoded. The German diplomatic systems of 1941 (Floradora and others) were partly read by GC&CS, so some texts may survive in HW 12; these US copies were not read. Distinct from catalogue 687 (two La Paz radiograms on MID cards, 1940-41). known.py: no hits for 862.20224.
why: A dense run of Axis legation code traffic from wartime Bolivia, obtained by informers and filed unread by the FBI and State Department; a test of what survives of German, Japanese and French diplomatic codes in Latin America, 1941-42.
prior_art: open (checked 27 Oct 2026: known.py, catalogue.json; the file is not online)

title: James Wilkinson ('Agent 13') ↔ Spanish governors of Louisiana: cipher letters in two dictionary-and-table codes, most pages unread
correspondents: James Wilkinson → Spanish governors of Louisiana / agents of the Spanish Crown (Miró, Carondelet, Gayoso; not itemised in the source), and replies
date: c. 1789-1806 (letters undated in the released transcriptions)
shelfmark: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, reproductions of the Archivo General de Indias, Papeles procedentes de Cuba, legajo 2374 (LoC page numbers 1524-1652, 2874-3072; 'File 1', 'File A', 'File B'); originals AGI Cuba leg. 2374
folio_note: Per the Chu/Valenti/Knight project inventory (github c2huc2hu/wilkinson data.txt): about 73 pp of ciphertext without decipherment and 28 pp with interlinear decipherment. Two systems: the '1078' code (table of ~1,240 numbered words with caret, plus page.row dictionary references with one or two bars for the column; dictionary ~780 pp x 2 cols x 29 rows) and a different '1096' system. Unsolved pages: LoC 1524, 1576-1583, 1598-1600, 1630-1631, 1642-1643, 2874, 2888-2890, 2895-2898, 2907-2909, 2930, 2943-2946, 2951-2953, 2962-2965, 2972, 3044-3047; decipherments for 1614-1624 and 1635-1637 exist (LoC 2975-2989, 3014-3018) but the project did not have the scans.
status: Partly read. Chu, Valenti and Knight (EMNLP Findings 2020, arXiv 2010.04746) recovered 75.1% of cipher-word tokens on a held-out 500-token excerpt (LoC 3044-3045) by a known-plaintext wordbank from the deciphered pages plus a neural LM; the dictionary itself was never identified and the 1096 system was not attacked. Not in the repo (known.py: no hits for 2374, Papeles de Cuba, Wilkinson cipher). Not on DECODE as far as checked.
why: Wilkinson's paid espionage for Spain while commanding the US Army is a major early-republic affair; the unread letters would document what he sold and when, including the Burr period.
language: English (some French words in the plaintext)
prior_art: partly read: Chu, Valenti & Knight 2020, 75.1% tokens on one excerpt; dictionary unidentified (checked 28 Oct 2026: arXiv paper, GitHub repo, web search; no later full reading found)

frame_check.saw: Searched loc.gov (Cloudflare check passed on waiting) and the c2huc2hu/wilkinson GitHub repo; found no loc.gov item or viewer for the Wilkinson/AGI cipher pages. Not viewed.
frame_check.note: Online location of the scans not found.
